### Misplaced Confidence
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/misplaced-confidence
Passage: Jeremiah 7:3-4
Points:
- The people of Judah placed false confidence in possessing the temple, assuming God would never permit Jerusalem to fall.
- Selectively reading God's promises while ignoring His covenant demands produces dangerous spiritual presumption.
- True faith must be demonstrated through love for God and active justice toward the needy and vulnerable.
- Outward religious privileges and holy places offer no protection to people living in unrepentant rebellion.
- Genuine assurance today rests not on a past ritual or decision, but on present, active trust in Christ.

### Read the Bible: Joshua 14–15, Psalms 146–147, Jer. 7, and Matthew 21
Author: D. A. Carson
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/devotionals/read-the-bible/josh-14-15-psalms-146-147-jeremiah-7-matt-21/
Passage: Jeremiah 7:1-15
Points:
- Chanting sacred phrases and relying on external religious institutions cannot shield unrepentant sinners from divine judgment.
- God requires genuine moral renewal, the rejection of idols, and active justice and generosity toward others.
- Severe hypocrisy arises when people commit gross sins and then treat the temple as a safe haven.
- Modern churchgoers easily make the same error by imagining modest religious observance makes them immune to judgment.
- Continual refusal to listen to God's repeated warnings eventually leads a society to spiritual ruin.

### Bible Pathways - Aug. 16, 2007
Author: Bible Pathway Ministries
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/biblepathways/bible-pathways-aug-16-2007-11549870.html
Passage: Jeremiah 7:1-11
Points:
- Outward participation in temple worship cannot substitute for a heart surrendered to God's commands.
- The people of Judah falsely believed their covenant heritage gave them license to persist in willful sin.
- Jeremiah rebuked those who committed theft, murder, and idolatry, yet claimed deliverance within God's sanctuary.
- Christ later quoted Jeremiah's temple rebuke to condemn religious leaders who turned God's house into a den of thieves.
- Genuine discipleship requires obedience to God's Word rather than reliance on mere religious titles and external rites.
